item.title: Mark Zuckerberg Reframes Meta's Superintelligence AI Strategy
item.description:
Meta reported a robust performance in Q2, achieving $47.5 billion in revenue and attracting nearly 3.5 billion daily users, leading to a more than 10% surge in stock value. In a strategic pivot, CEO Mark Zuckerberg has prioritized AI and superintelligence initiatives over previous metaverse ambitions. This change is already yielding positive results, with new AI models improving ad conversions by 3-5% on platforms like Facebook and Instagram.


Zuckerberg’s decision to not fully open source future advanced AI models reflects concerns about safety, marking a transition from Meta’s earlier stance on open-source AI exemplified by its Llama models. This shift comes as the company undertakes substantial investments in AI research, including $14.3 billion funneled into Scale AI and restructuring efforts under Meta Superintelligence Labs.


With Zuckerberg’s vision for ‘personal superintelligence,’ advanced AI is expected to be delivered through wearable AR glasses and VR headsets. Although this suggests a new monetization strategy centered on proprietary hardware, Meta is leveraging its profitable core business to fund the ambitious AI initiatives. Both Meta and Microsoft are forecasted to spend approximately $70 billion each on AI infrastructure within the current fiscal year amidst investor scrutiny. While AI investments have exhibited tangible benefits—improved ad targeting at Meta and enhanced cloud business growth at Microsoft—analysts pinpoint the necessity of demonstrating quicker sales growth relative to the substantial AI capital expenditure.


Zuckerberg foresees a future where AI glasses will be crucial, providing significant cognitive advantages. Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses have succeeded beyond expectations with a tripling in revenue year-over-year, even as Reality Labs incurred losses reaching $4.53 billion in Q2 and almost $70 billion since 2020. Despite the exploration of various AI wearables by competitors, Zuckerberg remains committed to glasses as the primary vehicle for merging the physical and digital realms, propelling the metaverse vision forward.


Through dedicated efforts, Zuckerberg aims for personalized superintelligent AI to empower rather than replace jobs, underscoring smart glasses as the future’s main computing devices. This stance sharpens the contrast with firms like OpenAI, who concentrate on automating work. Regardless, both Meta and OpenAI share the ultimate goal of providing personalized AI assistance.


In a landscape where rivals like Amazon and Microsoft navigate the AI investment terrain with differing results, Meta’s commitment to superintelligence represents a strategic bet on a transformative technology aimed at personal empowerment and enhanced user experience rather than purely automation.

item.title: Better Auth is so good that I **almost** switched programming languages
item.description: Better Auth is a TypeScript authentication library that offers comprehensive features like two-factor authentication, organizations, and payment integrations through plugins. While the author prefers Go for backend development, Better Auth's capabilities are compelling enough to consider switching languages. The tutorial demonstrates how to integrate Better Auth with a Go backend using JWT tokens, covering token generation, verification with JWK endpoints, and different approaches for authenticated requests including client-side caching and server-to-server proxying through Next.js.

item.title: Anthropic Introduces Weekly Rate Limits for Claude Code Subscribers
item.description:
Anthropic Introduces Weekly Rate Limits for Claude Code Subscribers


Anthropic has recently announced the introduction of weekly rate limits for its Claude Code service, effective August 28, 2025. These changes will impact both Pro and Max subscribers. This decision is part of a broader trend among AI companies to manage usage and computational resource constraints, although it has sparked discussions about fairness and transparency.


Background:


AI companies, including Anthropic, have historically offered subscriptions claiming “unlimited” access, only to later impose usage restrictions. This practice can be particularly frustrating for power users who have integrated these tools into their workflows, as it challenges the trust and commitment necessary for full organizational adoption.


New Limits Overview:


Under the new structure, Claude Code operates on a 5-hour rolling session model. Weekly quotas impact less than 5% of users who are known for intensive usage patterns, including those running the AI coding tool continuously and sharing accounts. Most users will receive 140-280 hours of Sonnet 4 and 15-35 hours of Opus 4 per week. Max subscribers can multiply their usage capacity with tiers priced at $100 and $200 per month, offering enhanced access including Opus 4.


Pricing Details:


Pro plans are priced at $20/month with capabilities for 10-40 prompts per session. API usage charges are standardized across platforms like Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI at $3/$15 per million tokens for Sonnet 4 and $15/$75 for Opus 4. Enterprise users have additional options to streamline control and observability through Portkey’s AI Gateway.


Criticism and Alternatives:


The adjustments have been met with criticism from developers, who argue that legitimate power users are unfairly penalized due to the actions of others abusing the system. Yet, Anthropic maintains that rate limits are necessary to ensure system reliability and to prevent policy violations that can disrupt service for all users. Comparatively, similar pricing strategies and restrictions have been adopted by other AI tool providers, including Cursor and Replit.


This change emphasizes the importance of transparent communication and clear expectations regarding usage policies for AI services. As computational demand grows, companies must balance access and performance while maintaining user trust.

item.title: The Useless useCallback
item.description: Many useCallback and useMemo implementations are pointless because they don't provide actual performance benefits. Memoization only helps when passing props to memoized components or preventing effects from firing unnecessarily. Common anti-patterns include memoizing functions passed to regular components and using non-primitive props as dependencies. The latest ref pattern and upcoming useEffectEvent can solve these issues without requiring extensive memoization chains.

item.title: JS 2025 just dropped with amazing features...
item.description: ECMAScript 2025 introduces several significant features including iterator helpers that provide lazy evaluation and functional operators for better performance, new set methods for intersection and difference operations, JSON module imports, RegExp.escape for preventing injection attacks, Promise.try for unified error handling, and Float16Array for memory-efficient numerical computing in high-performance applications.

item.title: Nitrode – AI Game Engine: AI Game Engine to Prototype 3D Games in a Day
item.description: Nitrode is an AI-powered game engine designed to help developers rapidly create playable 3D games within hours rather than weeks or months. The platform enables 'vibe coding' for quick prototyping, targeting developers who want to build games they've envisioned but lacked the time or resources to develop using traditional methods.

item.title: Self-Host Your Own Automation Platform with n8n + Docker
item.description: A comprehensive guide to setting up n8n, a self-hosted automation platform, using Docker Compose on Ubuntu Linux. The tutorial covers installation, configuration with PostgreSQL database, creating workflows that integrate with services like Discord and Google Sheets, and building advanced automations that incorporate local LLM models through Ollama for sentiment analysis. Demonstrates three workflow examples: basic Discord messaging, Google Sheets data processing with loops, and an advanced sentiment analysis pipeline that updates spreadsheet data using AI.

item.title: React Native Bootcamp in 30 HOURS for FREE 🎉
item.description: A comprehensive 30-hour React Native bootcamp that teaches mobile development through building six practical applications including a Twitter clone, recipe app, expense tracker, bookstore app, Instagram clone, and a full-stack todo application. The course covers React Native fundamentals, navigation, authentication, database integration, and deployment, designed for complete beginners with no prior mobile development experience.

item.title: Building competency is better than therapy
item.description: Building technical competency through learning programming, Linux, or contributing to open source projects can be more effective than traditional therapy for addressing mild depression. The combination of skill development, community engagement, and meaningful contribution creates a sense of purpose and flow that naturally counters negative mental states. Open source development particularly excels by offering endless learning opportunities, collaborative communities, and meaningful responsibilities that fulfill core human psychological needs.

item.title: What to Look for in Code Reviews
item.description: A comprehensive guide covering the essential aspects of effective code reviews, prioritized by importance. Covers design considerations as the most critical factor, followed by functionality review, complexity assessment, test quality evaluation, naming and documentation standards, and style consistency. Emphasizes the importance of structured approaches over random scanning, focusing on catching bugs, improving code quality, and facilitating team learning through systematic review practices.

item.title: Nova: The beautiful, fast, flexible, native Mac Code Editor
item.description: Nova is a native Mac code editor developed by Panic, emphasizing Mac-specific design and performance over cross-platform compatibility. It features deep Mac integration, custom text layout engine, flexible workflows, built-in terminals, and extension API. The editor focuses on traditional hand-typed coding rather than AI-assisted development, positioning itself as a modern alternative to cross-platform editors like VS Code.
